about: What calls on the runtime conformance plugin (conformance-weather) return: one list that both the real runtimes and the SDK testing tools are checked against (issue #206, risk A1, Q6.7.2).

Real runtimes: rutis_bridge::runtime::testing::runtime (crates/rutis-bridge/tests/session_matrix.rs). Testing tools: node/rutis/test/conformance.test.mjs (@arcships/rutis/testing) and python/rutis/tests/test_conformance.py (rutis.testing), in strict mode.
The plugin injects `clock`, whose `now()` returns 0, 1, 2, ... one per call, and provides `service` with `methods`.

A call: `call` (method), `args` (JSON; {"$callback": ...} is a function the caller passes: "upper" returns its argument upper-cased; {"throws": {name, message, fields}} throws an error with that name and message and extra `fields`), and what it does: `returns` (a JSON value; keys in `ignore` are not compared; `copied`: it is not the object passed in), `throws` ({} for any error, or the `name` and `message` the caller receives; the thrown error's extra `fields` do not cross) or `exits` (the plugin's process exits with this status).
`samples` are values one language makes: the plugin's `samples()` names the ones it has, `sample(name)` returns one; a runtime whose plugin has no `samples` method has none.
`allowed`: the testing tool does not do what this entry says, and why (a bounded, written-down difference, also in docs/guide/plugin-api.md). Every other entry holds for both.

calls.why: a sync call that calls a host service
the host service is called on every call
a callback during a sync call
an error crosses twice (callback to plugin, plugin to caller) with its name and message, not as the object thrown
data crosses both ways as a copy

calls.allowed: the testing tool runs the plugin in the test's own process, so a plugin that ends its process ends the test: the tool cannot show this, and tests do not call it

samples.why: binary data (a Uint8Array) does not cross
a number that is not finite does not cross
undefined inside data arrives as null
an Error returned as a value arrives as data: its name, message and stack
a tuple arrives as a list
a dataclass arrives as a dict
a float that is not finite does not cross
a dict with keys that are not strings does not cross
an exception returned as a value arrives as data: its name and message
